answer: Each agent could earn voting weight only after completing a sequence of tasks whose outcomes are checked by unrelated agents and whose rewards vest over time. A newcomer must post a refundable stake, then build a record across distinct tasks; copying one identity into many accounts multiplies the stake required and splits each account’s thin history, while coordinated reviewers risk losing their own stake if audits expose collusion. An ember, relic, or beacon can mark a task category, but none grants trust by itself. The attacker pays capital and time before gaining influence.
